title: URL Shortener
brief: Design a service that turns a long web address into a short one, like sho.rt/aZ3k, and sends anyone who opens the short link to the original page. Far more people will open links than create them, and a link must keep working for years.

functional: Create a short link for a long URL.
Open a short link and be redirected to the long URL.
Let the creator choose a custom alias.
Let links expire after a set time.
Show the owner how many times a link was opened.

nonFunctional.name: Latency
nonFunctional.target: A redirect takes under 50 ms at the 99th percentile

nonFunctional.name: Durability
nonFunctional.target: A link never disappears once created

nonFunctional.name: Codes
nonFunctional.target: Short, 7 characters, and not guessable one by one

estimate.note: Links are tiny, so storage stays small. Traffic shapes the design: far more people open links than create them.

outputs.label: Opens per second, average
outputs.note: Peak is often 2 to 5 times this.

outputs.label: Base-62 characters needed
outputs.note: 62 characters: a to z, A to Z, 0 to 9.

api.does: Creates a link and returns the short code.
Redirects to the long URL. 404 if unknown, 410 if expired.
Returns open counts for the owner.

data.why: Every read is one lookup by code, with no joins.
Written in batches by a worker, never on the redirect path.

evolution.title: One server
evolution.problem: Start with the simplest thing that works: one app server and one database.
evolution.change: Create a code, store code to URL, and look it up on every open.

evolution.title: Load balancer
evolution.problem: One server is a single point of failure, and reads are the heavy part.
evolution.change: Run several identical stateless app servers behind a load balancer.

evolution.title: Cache
evolution.problem: Opens outnumber creates by 100 to 1, and a few links get most of them.
evolution.change: Check a cache before the database and fill it on a miss.
evolution.numbers: most opens end at the cache

evolution.title: Unique codes
evolution.problem: Two app servers must never hand out the same code.
evolution.change: An ID service gives each server a block of unused numbers. The code is the number in base 62.

evolution.title: Shard the store
evolution.problem: Terabytes of links will not fit or be served by one database.
evolution.change: Split links across databases by code so each holds a slice.
evolution.numbers: the estimator shows how many TB

evolution.title: Count clicks off the path
evolution.problem: Owners want counts, but writing a count on every open would slow the redirect.
evolution.change: Drop a click event on a queue. A worker adds them up later.

steps.say: The client sends the long URL to the service.
The load balancer picks any app server. They are all the same.
The server takes the next number from its ID block. No database round trip, no collision.
It writes the number as base 62. That is the short code.
It stores code to long URL on the shard that owns that code.
The short link goes back to the client.
The load balancer sends it to an app server.
The server checks the cache first. Most opens end here.
On a miss it reads the shard that owns this code.
It fills the cache so the next open is a hit.
It drops a click event on the queue and does not wait for it.
It answers with a redirect to the long URL.

deepDives.title: Making the short code
deepDives.question: How do we make a code that is short, never collides and is cheap to create?

options.name: Hash the URL, keep a prefix
options.pros: Same URL gives the same code, so duplicates are free to detect.
options.cons: A short prefix collides. Each collision needs a check and a retry.

options.name: Random code, check it is free
options.cons: Every create needs a read to check for a clash. It gets slower as the table fills.

options.name: Unique number, written in base 62
options.pros: No collisions, no check, very fast.
options.cons: Codes are in order and guessable. Needs an ID service.

deepDives.because: Creation stays cheap and always succeeds. To stop people guessing the next code, scramble the number with a secret reversible mix before encoding.

deepDives.title: Which redirect
deepDives.question: Should the redirect be 301 (permanent) or 302 (temporary)?

options.name: 301 permanent
options.pros: Browsers remember it, so much less traffic reaches us.
options.cons: We never see repeat opens, so click counts are wrong. We cannot change the target.

options.name: 302 temporary
options.pros: Every open reaches us, so counts and edits work.
options.cons: More traffic for the cache to absorb.

deepDives.because: Owners want click counts and the right to change a link. The cache makes the extra traffic cheap.

deepDives.title: Where links are stored
deepDives.question: Relational database or key-value store?

options.name: Relational
options.pros: Familiar, strong guarantees, easy ad hoc queries.

options.name: Key-value store
options.pros: One-key lookups scale out by adding nodes.
options.cons: Little support for queries across links.

deepDives.because: Every read and write is by code. There are no joins to lose, and sharding comes built in.

failures.impact: Every open hits the database, so latency jumps and the database may fall over.
failures.fix: Run cache replicas. Limit how many misses reach the database at once. Size the database to survive a cold cache for a short while.

failures.impact: No new links can be created.
failures.fix: Each app server holds a spare block, so short outages go unnoticed. Run the ID service on several nodes.

failures.impact: One shard gets hammered by the same code.
failures.fix: The cache absorbs most of it. Replicate that key, and add read replicas for the shard.

failures.what: People use it to hide malware
failures.impact: Short links hide where they lead, so the service gets abused.
failures.fix: Scan new URLs, let people report links, expire suspicious ones, and limit creation per user.

scaling.lever: Place codes on shards with consistent hashing, so adding a shard moves only a slice of the codes.

scaling.limit: Users are spread across the world
scaling.lever: Add regional caches and read replicas, and route each user to the nearest one.

recap.key: Opens vastly outnumber creates, so cache hard. Make codes from unique numbers in base 62 so they never collide.
recap.numbers: About 100 creates and 10K opens per second. A few TB over 5 years. 7 base-62 characters cover 3.5 trillion links.
moves: Estimate first: reads outnumber writes 100 to 1
Make codes from an ID block in base 62
Cache the reads and shard the store by code
Count clicks through a queue, off the redirect path
